name: GW0742
lead: GW0742 (also GW610742 and proposed trade name fitorine) is an investigational PPAR-delta (PPAR-beta/delta) agonist developed by GlaxoSmithKline and used widely as a laboratory tool compound. It is not an approved medicine.[1][2]

Appearance interest follows a chain: PPAR-delta activation drives fatty-acid oxidation and glucose uptake in muscle and fat in laboratory models -> the compound is discussed as a way to support fat loss and endurance -> leaner body composition. Grokipedia reports that it is sold gray-market to bodybuilders and athletes as "Cardarine 2.0", positioned as an alternative to the related compound GW501516.[2][10]

Published research on GW0742 consists of cell and animal studies of inflammation, cardiovascular disease, liver fat and metabolism. Researchers have also flagged concerns, drawn from rodent work on its analogue GW501516, about tumour promotion.[2]

paras: GW0742 is a thiazole-based compound with a phenoxyacetic acid side chain, structurally related to GW501516.[2] Its formula is C21H17F4NO3S2 and its molar mass is about 471 g/mol.[1] Medicinal chemists have made derivatives, including one swapping the thiazole for an oxazole that inhibited vitamin D receptor-mediated transcription.[1]

A 2003 paper from the GSK-linked group described the synthesis and biological activity of novel selective PPAR-delta agonists, naming GW501516 and GW0742 as optimised leads with low-nanomolar potency and high selectivity over other human PPAR subtypes.[3]

PPAR-delta is a nuclear receptor that regulates genes for lipid metabolism, energy balance and inflammation.[2][11] Grokipedia gives an EC50 of about 3.7 nM at human PPAR-delta with over 300-fold selectivity over the alpha and gamma subtypes, while Wikipedia notes that GW0742 can behave as an agonist or antagonist depending on dose and has weak activity at other nuclear receptors, including androgen and vitamin D receptors.[1][2]
A 2023 review of PPARs in fatty liver disease notes that PPAR-beta/delta agonists have been proposed to improve insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism disorders.[11]

In obese diabetic mice, PPAR-delta activation induced insulin-induced gene-1 and suppressed hepatic lipogenesis.[7] GW610742 reduced cholesterol absorption in mice alongside decreased intestinal NPC1L1 expression.[12] Work in primary human myotubes reported direct activation of glucose transport after PPAR-delta activation.[13] A protective role against hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion injury was reported in mice in 2023.[14]

GW0742 and GW501516 inhibited TNF-alpha-induced adhesion molecule expression in human vascular endothelial cells, and PPAR-delta activation reduced angiotensin II-accelerated atherosclerosis in mice.[4][5] In rats after myocardial infarction, GW610742 raised angiogenesis and fibrosis at one week without differences in cardiac function through four weeks.[15] In diabetic mice, GW0742 was examined against inflammation and fibrosis in diabetic cardiomyopathy.[16] Wikipedia lists mouse studies on pancreatitis and diet-induced hypertension.[1]

In a study including sebocyte cultures and patient comparisons, the PPAR-delta agonist GW0742 increased lipogenesis in SEB-1 sebocytes, as did agonists of other PPAR subtypes, while isotretinoin decreased it; the paper reports human sebum production increases in patients taking PPAR-gamma or PPAR-alpha drugs.[6]

In neonatal rats, intranasal GW0742 reduced mast cell degranulation and neurological impairment after germinal matrix haemorrhage.[17] Other work examined colon carcinogenesis and cell differentiation with PPAR-beta/delta ligands.[8][9]

No studies found. Published research is limited to cell-based and animal work.[3][4][5][6][7] GW501516, the related compound, reached phase I and II trials at GlaxoSmithKline before development ended in 2007.[10]

GW0742 is sold in bodybuilding and athletic circles as "Cardarine 2.0", "Super Cardarine" or "Advanced Cardio".[2] Grokipedia describes anecdotal preferences, with GW0742 favoured by some for fat loss and GW501516 for endurance, and states that no human data establish either claim.[2]

On T Nation, one poster listed GW501516, GW0742 and telmisartan as the known PPAR-delta agonists in a fat-loss thread, and another said GW0742 and GW501516 are reported to aid recovery while noting that people worry about cancer with GW501516 and consider GW0742 "supposedly safer".[18][19]

WADA added GW501516 and related PPAR-delta modulators to its prohibited list in 2009, and in 2013 warned of health risks, saying clinical approval had not and would not be given for GW501516.[10] Athletes have been sanctioned for GW501516 use,[10] and GW0742 is not an approved medicine anywhere.

Animal testing of GW501516 later showed rapid cancer development in several organs in mice and rats, and GSK dropped development in 2007.[10] Grokipedia applies this concern to GW0742 and states that its long-term human safety is unknown.[2]

timeline.event: Selective PPAR-delta agonists, including GW0742, described in a medicinal chemistry paper.[3]
GSK ends development of the related GW501516 after phase II studies.[10]
WADA prohibits PPAR-delta modulators such as GW501516.[10]

card.summary: A GSK PPAR-delta research compound sold gray-market as "Cardarine 2.0", with lab and animal data only and no human trials.
card.note: Not approved; analogue GW501516 promoted tumour growth in rodent studies and long-term human safety is unknown.

quick.overview:
GW0742 is a selective PPAR-delta agonist made by GlaxoSmithKline and used mostly as a lab tool. Some bodybuilding and fat-loss communities market it as a stronger sibling of GW501516.

Published research is cell and animal work on inflammation, metabolism and the heart; no human trials were found.
quick.mechanism: It activates PPAR-delta, a nuclear receptor involved in fatty acid oxidation, glucose handling and inflammation, in laboratory models.
quick.risks: It is not an approved medicine and human safety data are lacking. Rodent studies of the related GW501516 reported tumour promotion, and that concern is cited for GW0742 as well.

chain: Activates PPAR-delta in muscle, fat and liver
Shifts tissues toward fatty-acid oxidation in lab models
Discussed as supporting leanness and endurance
angle.text: People in fat-loss and endurance circles talk about GW0742 because PPAR-delta activation raises fat burning in cells and animals. Its use for physique goals rests on that laboratory biology; no human study has measured body composition with it.
